extracted.intended_audience: researchers, companies, and organizations planning to submit proposals to ARPA-H funding opportunities
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step guidance for finding, preparing, submitting, and negotiating ARPA-H funding opportunities (ISOs, Programs, Initiatives, SBIR/STTR), including account/registration, Solution Summaries, solicitation compliance, and post-award expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read and follow the solicitation in its entirety
rubrics_metrics.description: A solicitation is the official announcement inviting submissions and details opportunity information, technical requirements, eligibility, key dates, submission process, evaluation criteria, formatting requirements and templates, policy requirements, and any additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is extremely important that proposers read the solicitation and its associated documents in their entirety, understand the technical requirements, and follow all instructions. ARPA-H may not review submissions that are missing required documents, don’t address the requirements, are longer than the page limit allowed, or are in alternative templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the most up-to-date solicitation documents and monitor amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicitations may be amended and key dates/deadlines may change during the solicitation period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bookmark opportunities, consider 'following' the contract opportunity on SAM.gov, use SAM.gov 'View Changes' to highlight recent changes, and download documents with recent changes (updated documents typically include an amendment date in the file name). Continue referencing the solicitation throughout the period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locate solicitation attachments on SAM.gov (or follow special posting instructions)
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-H posts and maintains most solicitations on SAM.gov; a direct link will be on the ARPA-H opportunity informational page. Look for the solicitation PDF and zip file of additional documents in the 'Attachment' section on SAM.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In instances when solicitations are posted/maintained outside SAM.gov, the opportunity’s informational page will provide further instructions. Check for related notices that may include Proposers’ Day details when posted separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create and use an ARPA-H Solutions site account when required
rubrics_metrics.description: The Solutions site is ARPA-H's submission and registration platform where proposers can ask questions, register for events, create teaming profiles, and submit Solution Summaries and proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some solicitations may not require a Solutions site account—confirm in the solicitation. Familiarize yourself with site features; note the system currently does not allow edits to submitted summaries or proposals. Use the Solve site’s 'Ask A Question' form for inquiries after submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain and maintain required entity registrations (UEI and SAM.gov)
rubrics_metrics.description: All solicitations require a valid Unique Entity ID (UEI) at the time of proposal submission; prior to award, all proposers must complete and maintain SAM.gov registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some solicitations may require active SAM.gov registration at submission. Start the registration early because it can take several weeks. If previously registered, verify entity information is accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow formatting, page limits, templates, and proprietary information instructions exactly
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission documents and templates will include instructions on required content, page length, font, font size, margin widths, how to address proprietary information, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that do not follow requirements may not be reviewed. Ensure you are using the most updated documents and templates specified in the solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand and address the evaluation criteria listed in the solicitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation criteria and information about the review process are included in the solicitation and will be used to assess proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is very important that proposers understand the evaluation criteria and carefully prepare submission materials accordingly. If not selected, proposers may request an informal feedback session based on the evaluation criteria provided in the solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit a Solution Summary (recommended or required) before a full proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: A Solution Summary is a short concept submission that allows ARPA-H to provide feedback on relevance and viability prior to investing resources in a full proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some opportunities require proposers to submit a Solution Summary and receive feedback before submitting a proposal; ARPA-H will only review proposals when the required Solution Summary has been reviewed and feedback provided. Even when not required, ARPA-H recommends submitting a Solution Summary; only submit a full proposal if the Solution Summary feedback is 'encouraged.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect limited pre-proposal feedback (outside of Solution Summaries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outside of Solution Summary submissions, ARPA-H does not have capacity to provide feedback prior to submitting a proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Solution Summaries to obtain pre-proposal guidance. Questions submitted via the ARPA-H informational page may be generalized and added to public FAQs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget realistically with clear rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection decisions consider both availability of funds and the reasonableness of the proposed budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Price proposals appropriately for the proposer/organization and include strong rationale to account for estimates or anticipated risks. Unreasonable budgets can harm selection chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form teaming relationships when appropriate and use teaming profiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaming with other individuals/organizations expands expertise and is often necessary for Program-specific openings; ARPA-H recommends (but does not require) forming teams with varied technical expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opportunity pages will include a link to a teaming profiles page; interested parties can fill out a Teaming Profile Form on the ARPA-H Solutions site and, once approved, appear publicly on the arpa-h.gov site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ARPA-H outreach (Proposers’ Day, FAQs, 'Ask A Question') to learn and clarify
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-H offers optional Proposers’ Day events, opportunity-specific FAQs, and question submission forms to help proposers learn about opportunities and clarify requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers’ Day requires advanced registration and may not be offered for some ISOs or opportunities. FAQs are updated throughout the application process; questions submitted may be generalized and added to FAQ pages for the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware ARPA-H seeks revolutionary ideas and uses aggressive milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-H seeks revolutionary ideas; metrics and scope to receive funding are intentionally aggressive and ARPA-H uses outcome-based funding agreements with aggressive milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only submit proposals aligned to ARPA-H’s mission and research model. Consider that ARPA-H funds are performance-based and continuation may depend on meeting aggressive milestones and deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand submission immutability and timeliness (no edits allowed after submit)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARPA-H Solutions site currently does not allow editing submitted Solution Summaries or proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submissions are final and accurate before submission. Use the 'Ask A Question' form for follow-up inquiries after submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare for negotiation content and documentation if selected
rubrics_metrics.description: If selected for negotiations, ARPA-H and the proposer will negotiate terms including scope of work, project duration/schedule, success metrics, performance-based milestones, budget, team composition, intellectual property, and required compliance/regulatory considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negotiations often involve requests for clarifications or additional documentation; proposers may update proposed work to ensure alignment with Program objectives, milestones, schedule, or budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate research security review for recommended proposals (except most SBIR/STTR)
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of proposals submitted through small business SBIRs or STTRs, all proposals recommended for funding will go through a research security review handled separately and in parallel with other award negotiations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for this separate review and ensure compliance with any security-related requirements spelled out in solicitation and agency guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know typical award instruments and performance expectations (OTs and Cooperative Agreements)
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-H primarily awards Other Transactions (OTs) and Cooperative Agreements for R&D, which are different from grants and are often performance-based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding allocations and continuation on projects are contingent on meeting agreed-upon milestones. ARPA-H provides support for OT planning, execution, and administration; learn more via ARPA-H resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award execution: meet milestones, maintain communication, and comply with terms
rubrics_metrics.description: After award, performers are expected to execute the proposed project plan, meet aggressive milestones and deliverables, maintain regular communication with Project Managers, provide progress reports, participate in status meetings, and promptly communicate significant issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PMs will monitor progress and may work with performers to pivot, downselect, or remove/modify unsuccessful aspects. Performers must comply with contractual, regulatory, and reporting requirements including financial management, data sharing, and ethical, safety, and security protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand selection outcomes and post-decision options
rubrics_metrics.description: After review, proposers will receive notification indicating 'selected for negotiation,' 'not selected for negotiation,' or a 'partial selection.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not selected, proposers may request an informal feedback session based on the solicitation’s evaluation criteria. Timing for responses may vary with submission volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow solicitation-specific exceptions and instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Some solicitations may have additional steps or different submission requirements (e.g., no Solutions site account required; Mission Office ISOs accepted on a rolling basis and may not have Proposers’ Days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always check the associated solicitation for full, up-to-date information; rely on solicitation text when there are differences from general guidance.
